agent-x.takeaway: LLM agents judge a text against routed stylistic guidelines, and a meta agent merges their calibrated verdicts, so no detection threshold is tuned. AGENT-X has the highest average accuracy for all four source models tested; Fast-DetectGPT keeps the higher average AUROC.
agent-x.question: Score-based detectors such as Fast-DetectGPT need a threshold, tuned on labeled data, before they can call a text AI-generated or human-written, and the threshold may not transfer to a new domain. Can a detector reach the label directly, explain it, and stay accurate without a calibration set?

glance.result: Highest average accuracy for all four source models; on GPT-4 texts, 0.8592 vs 0.6800 for the best baseline, Likelihood.
glance.prior: Likelihood, LogRank, and Fast-DetectGPT output scores that need a tuned threshold; AGENT-X returns a label with a rationale.
glance.limitation: By AUROC, which needs no threshold, Fast-DetectGPT averages higher for all four source models (GPT-4: 0.9061 vs 0.9007).

agent-x.prior_work: Zero-shot detectors score a text with a language model. Likelihood, Rank, LogRank, Entropy, and LRR use token statistics; DetectGPT and NPR compare the text with perturbed copies; DNA-GPT compares it with regenerated continuations; Fast-DetectGPT (Bao et al., 2024) replaces DetectGPT's perturbations with a cheaper sampling step. Supervised classifiers such as the RoBERTa detectors and GPTZero need labeled training data, and watermarking needs control over generation. A score becomes a label only after a threshold is chosen. AGENT-X prompts an LLM with explicit guidelines instead, and calibrates the model's verbalized confidence with SteeringConf (Zhou et al., 2025), a method that queries the same model under several confidence-steering prompts.

diagram.title: From guidelines to a label without a threshold

steps.label: Route
steps.text: Infer the text's domain and style; activate only the guidelines that match.

steps.label: Judge
steps.text: One agent per guideline; five steering prompts calibrate its confidence.

steps.label: Aggregate
steps.text: A meta agent weighs the reports by confidence and returns the label.

diagram.caption: Every stage is an LLM call; the final label is the meta agent's decision, not a thresholded score.

method.title: Route guidelines to the text
method.text: An LLM infers the text's domain and stylistic features, then activates only the matching guidelines in each of the semantic, stylistic, and structural dimensions (25 guidelines in total).

method.title: Judge each guideline five times
method.text: A base agent labels the text under one guideline with each steering prompt, from very cautious to very confident. Answer agreement and confidence spread shrink the mean confidence into a calibrated score.

method.title: Aggregate with a meta agent
method.text: A meta agent reads all guideline reports, gives more weight to confident agents, and returns the final label, a rationale, and a confidence calibrated with the same five steering prompts.

findings.label: GPT-4 · PubMed accuracy: AGENT-X vs Fast-DetectGPT
findings.detail: Fast-DetectGPT's threshold was tuned on SQuAD texts from GPT-Neo-2.7B. By AUROC, which needs no threshold, it scores slightly higher than AGENT-X (0.8503 vs 0.8447; Tables 1 and 5).

findings.label: GPT-4 average accuracy: AGENT-X vs the best baseline, Likelihood
findings.detail: AGENT-X has the highest average accuracy for all four source models; its smallest margin is on Claude-3-Sonnet (0.8000 vs 0.7856 for Likelihood, +1.44 pp; Tables 1 and 2).

findings.label: GPT-4 average accuracy without the guidelines
findings.detail: Replacing the guidelines with randomly selected prompts lowers accuracy from 0.8592 to 0.6139, the largest drop among five ablations; uncalibrated confidences cost 6.01 pp (Table 3).

agent-x.scope: All agents run on one LLM, deepseek-chat-v3-0324, and the evaluation covers three datasets from the Fast-DetectGPT benchmark (XSum, WritingPrompts, PubMedQA) with texts from four commercial source models. Baseline thresholds come from a single out-of-domain validation set. The paper reports no sample counts, run-to-run variance, or cost, supports its interpretability claim with one worked case, and announces but does not link a code and guideline release in v1.

results_table.caption: Table 3 (all rows; the per-dataset AUROC columns are omitted). Ablations of AGENT-X on GPT-4-generated texts: accuracy (ACC) per dataset and averaged, and average AUROC; higher is better. The change column is computed here as the difference in average accuracy from the full system. On XSum, two variants are more accurate than the full system (0.8691 vs 0.8624).
